question: GQ-001
subject: a gate that reported itself clean having examined zero files
method: starved each gate of its input and read what it did — a grep for guard wording scored two gates at 0, but only ONE of them was actually defective

the_defect.behaviour: run against a directory with an empty sources/, printed checked_files: 0, findings: [], sanity: "catalogue tables confirmed present", exit 0
the_defect.the_irony: this gate already warns when one of ITS rules names a missing table — "so it can no longer detect anything" — and did not apply that reasoning to itself
the_defect.evidence_was_in_its_own_output: checked_files: 0 was printed on every run and nothing acted on it

the_fix: emit a no-source-files-checked finding when zero files are read, so --strict exits 6

a_gate_that_did_NOT_need_fixing.first_result: exit 1 on empty input — but from a CRASH on a missing schema file, so my test never reached the claims
a_gate_that_did_NOT_need_fixing.retested_properly: with schema + portfolio + ledger present and claims/ empty, it exits 1 having detected that all 10 portfolio-listed claims are absent
a_gate_that_did_NOT_need_fixing.conclusion: a genuine cross-check, not vacuous passing — left alone
